title: Phaseout of Legacy GraphQL Admin API — migration roadmap, compatibility contract, and acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Executive summary: We will retire the Legacy GraphQL Admin API (graph-admin.v1) and migrate internal and customer-integrated clients to the Unified Admin REST API (admin.v2) and the GraphQL-lite read-only facade. The legacy API has operational complexity, inconsistent auth semantics with the Console, and prevents unified SDK improvements. This ticket defines requirements, scoped deliverables, rollout phases, and acceptance criteria for deprecation and migration assistance.
scope:
- Publish a detailed migration guide and automated CLI refactor tool.
- Provide a compatibility shim (deployment-side) for 12 weeks of traffic fallthrough in Redwood-hosted environments.
- Ship SDK updates with deprecation warnings and automatic rewrites for the most-common query patterns.
- Telemetry gates and regression checks to prevent content/permission regressions.
- Customer outreach cadence and self-serve notes for enterprise customers.
out_of_scope:
- On-prem private deployments where customers manage their own GraphQL servers (handled via separate Private upgrade advisory).
- Rewriting customer-owned integrations; we will provide migration tools and runbooks but not perform custom migrations unless covered by a paid concierge engagement.
migration_steps:
1) Publish PRD and migration playbook to Console docs and Support KB (owner: PM).
2) Implement server-side compatibility shim that translates graph-admin.v1 calls to admin.v2 for select endpoints (owner: Backend Eng).
3) Release SDK v3.1 with opt-in auto-migration flag and clear console warnings (owner: SDK team).
4) Provide CLI tool (redwood-migrate-admin) that analyzes GraphQL queries and outputs admin.v2 calls or GraphQL-lite equivalents (owner: DX).
5) Run 4-week shadowing (mirror requests to both endpoints) for internal customers and 2 pilot external customers.
6) Gradual throttling and quota limits on legacy API with detailed telemetry. Enable 12-week compatibility fallback with circuit breaker.
7) Enforce read-only sunset for write endpoints at final phase, then remove public discovery and issue final cutoff.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (Docs & Tools) - Weeks 0-2: Publish guides, CLI beta, SDK opt-in.
Phase B (Shim & Shadow) - Weeks 2-6: Deploy compatibility shim to hosted environments; enable shadowing and monitor.
Phase C (Customer Pilots) - Weeks 6-10: Engage 2-3 enterprise pilots, iterate compatibility and edge cases.
Phase D (Controlled Throttle) - Weeks 10-16: Introduce rate-limits and deprecation headers; open support channels.
Phase E (Cutover & Removal) - Week 20: Final cutoff for public legacy GraphQL endpoints after all gates green.

Note: Dates are target and gated on telemetry and pilot signoffs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Migration docs published and validated by Solutions Engineering.
- SDK v3.1 published with deprecation warnings and >=95% unit test coverage for migrated helpers.
- Compatibility shim passes smoke tests for top 25 query shapes (as measured by production request distribution).
- No permission/authorization regressions in pilot customers (zero P0 regressions in 4-week pilot).
- Telemetry gates: token-level rejection rates, 95th latency, and error budget OK for admin.v2 for 2 consecutive weeks.
- At least one enterprise pilot has completed migration using the CLI or SDK helpers.
- Customer-facing deprecation emails and Console banners scheduled 6 weeks before public throttle.
monitoring_and_telemetry:
Required signals:
- Legacy GraphQL request volume by operation name.
- Error rate and 5xx breakdown by translated shim vs native admin.v2.
- Auth/permission mismatch incidents (count + sample traces).
- SDK telemetry: % of clients using auto-migrate flag, warnings emitted.
- Customer migration progress dashboard: pilot status, endpoints remaining, and API key usage.
Telemetry owners: Observability team. Set SLOs and alerting for spike in legacy error classes.
communications_plan:
- Internal: All-hands email to Support/SE/Account teams week of 2025-03-17; weekly sync with Sales for enterprise plans.
- External: Console banner + in-product migration module, targeted emails to customers using graph-admin.v1, Playbook for CSMs.
- Public changelog and FAQ with migration examples and common gotchas.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Incomplete coverage of ad-hoc GraphQL queries used by customers. Mitigation: CLI analyzer to classify queries and recommend transformations; pilot with customers who have custom queries.
Risk: Auth surface differences cause permission errors. Mitigation: Dedicated auth compatibility tests, shadowing with sampled tokens.
Risk: SDK automatic rewrites introduce subtle semantics drift. Mitigation: Opt-in flag, experimental release, and rollback path.
Risk: High customer effort to migrate. Mitigation: Provide migration concierge for top 10 accounts and conversion scripts for common integrations.
notes:
- We must coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams for customers running self-managed control planes; advisory docs required.
- Budget for a 2-person concierge engagement for up to 8 weeks allocated from FY25 migration reserve.
- If pilot feedback shows more than 5 high-risk query patterns, pause throttle and extend shim window by 6 weeks.
